corpus: LOSS RESERVE ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM. Prepared by the Actuarial Reserving Committee for the Year-End 2024 statutory valuation. This memorandum documents the indicated and carried reserves for three lines of business, Commercial Auto Liability, Workers' Compensation, and General Liability, each evaluated as of December 31, 2024. SECTION I, COMMERCIAL AUTO LIABILITY. For accident year 2023, the net loss ratio for Commercial Auto Liability was 68.4 percent. For accident year 2024, the net loss ratio for Commercial Auto Liability was 71.2 percent. The combined ratio for Commercial Auto Liability was 97.6 percent. The carried reserve for Commercial Auto Liability, net of reinsurance, is $142.5 million. The age-to-ultimate development factor for Commercial Auto Liability is 1.0450. The discount rate applied to Commercial Auto Liability reserves is 275 basis points. SECTION II, WORKERS' COMPENSATION. For accident year 2023, the net loss ratio for Workers' Compensation was 61.9 percent. For accident year 2024, the net loss ratio for Workers' Compensation was 59.3 percent. The combined ratio for Workers' Compensation was 94.1 percent. The carried reserve for Workers' Compensation, gross of reinsurance, is $310.8 million. The average claim severity for Workers' Compensation is $42,300. The confidence level of the Workers' Compensation reserve estimate, held at the 80th percentile of the distribution, is 80 percent. SECTION III, GENERAL LIABILITY. The combined ratio for General Liability was 103.5 percent. The carried reserve for General Liability is approximately $87.2 million. The reserving basis for General Liability is the Bornhuetter-Ferguson method.
